# Threads {#sec-threads}

Environments share nothing, so threads that each use their own environment need no coordination.

## Sharing an environment {#sec-threads-sharing}

Threads may share one environment under these rules:

- Calls on different models may run at the same time, and so may calls that only read the same model.
- A call that changes a model runs alone on it. So do evaluating a model and reading one of its derivative patterns.
- A call that changes the environment, such as setting an option or adding a hook, runs alone on the environment and all its models. Creating or copying a model onto it is not such a change.
- `BIYOS_interrupt` and `BIYOS_lasterror` may run at any time.

A call that would break a rule fails at once with `BIYOS_ERR_BUSY`. It never waits, and it changes nothing, so the thread may try again once the other call has returned. Two calls that start at the same moment may both be refused, and a change may keep being refused while other threads keep calling. A program that changes a shared model or environment orders those changes itself.

Free a model or an environment only once no other thread is in a call on it or will make one. A free is refused while another call runs, but nothing can refuse a call that starts after the free.

To change one model from several threads, give each thread its own copy ([Copying models](#sec-copy)). Each thread has its own last error ([The last error](#sec-errors-message)).

## Evaluating on several threads {#sec-threads-evaluation}

An evaluation shares its work among as many threads as the option [`threads`](#opt-threads) says, 1 by default. Every count gives the same result, bit for bit. Callbacks run on the thread that made the call. While one model evaluates on the environment's threads, an evaluation of another model runs on its calling thread alone.

## Hooks {#sec-threads-hooks}

A hook runs on the thread whose call sent the event. The hooks of an environment run one at a time, so they need no lock among themselves. The hooks of a model also run one at a time, but beside those of other models and of the environment, so data shared with them needs a lock.

A hook must not wait for a call on another thread that sends it an event, since that call waits for the hook. For the same reason, hooks of two environments must not call into each other from two threads.

## Interrupting a call {#sec-threads-interrupt}

`BIYOS_interrupt` asks the calls running on an environment to stop. Any thread may call it, and so may a signal handler or a hook. A call stops only for a request made after it started, and ends with the termination `BIYOS_TRM_STOP`, which is an outcome, not an error code. See [`BIYOS_interrupt`](#BIYOS_interrupt).

## In Python {#sec-threads-python}

The package releases the interpreter lock during each C call, so threads that work on separate environments run side by side. Use one environment and its models from one thread at a time.

```{.python file="examples/code/python/threads.py"}
```

Each thread builds its own model on its own environment. A hook written in Python takes the interpreter lock while it runs.

`Env.interrupt` makes the same request from another thread. A `KeyboardInterrupt` raised in a hook makes it too, and is raised again once the call returns.
